analysis:
Reviewed all three batch analyses against the replayed patches and changelog. The executable change is confined to .github/workflows/release-provider.yml:239–242 (head): qualify-sdk now explicitly sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=prod. The build-provider job retains its resolved release environment; its changed lines 181–182 are commentary. docs/operations/provider-release.md:315–318 and changelog.d/qualify-sdk-prod-identity.md:3 document the production-default test configuration rather than introduce additional controls.
No independently supported security regression was identified. Selecting production defaults for qualification does not itself confer production credentials, approve a signed artifact, or grant coordinator serving authorization. The relevant security contracts are exact-artifact qualification and code identity (A-011, A-017, T-054), and the separation of diagnostic/test evidence from permission (TB-011, T-052, T-056). The patches do not alter transport encryption, plaintext handling, cache isolation, billing, logout, local hold admission or privileged-helper authority.
A material integration question remains: the local reviews report that provider-release-build also receives the resolved lane environment at workflow head:252–255. Its implementation and provider-swift/Package.swift are not replayed, so precedence between that input and the new job environment cannot be verified. Confirm that the override produces production-default qualification tests while preserving the selected environment of the separately built release artifact, and that environment-sensitive identity behavior remains adequately validated. This is an unverified contract, not evidence of a qualification bypass. Replay omits six reviewed source units, so surrounding signing, cache and packaged-smoke assertions in the prior analyses could not be independently rechecked here.
